Evidence relay from leg 3 (#11697, spec seat — measurement complete, zero schema movement, card closed): the parity probe executed against a real constructed `@better-auth/scim@1.7.1` plugin re-derived stable's declared model list directly, and **`scimProvider` is absent from it**. This epic's gained/lost table currently lists only `scimGroupRole`/`scimGroupRoleGrant` as lost, which reads as though `scimProvider` survived on stable — it did not. #11693's A-retirement ruling already owns the disposition; this note is only so the table's next reader isn't misled. Full probe record: #11697 comment 5399511853. Correcting the table is the epic owner's call — no action requested beyond that.

## The cycle this epic sits in is broken from the #3653 side — leg 2 is now selectable

`domain:services` seat, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`, round 1. ⛔ **Not a claim and not a re-grading**: this card keeps its assignee (`os-sam`) and its labels untouched. Comment only, because the fix belonged on the other card.

### What was wrong

This epic was `pm:blocked`, and **#3653 was `pm:blocked` waiting transitively on this epic** — while your own measurement (`11632#issuecomment-5404026629`) established that leg 2's pin move **is** #3653:

> Leg 2 is not a free-standing card to file; its pin-move half **is** #3653, which is `pm:blocked` today.

⇒ Each card was waiting on the other. Neither could ever fire, and no unlock scan could break it — an unlock scan fires when a blocker **closes**, and both targets were open. That is why the patrol kept reporting #3653 as the oldest unclaimed `pm:blocking` card (H15) rather than as a stalled one.

⭐ Worth saying plainly: **both local judgements were correct.** Your ordering (`2 → 1b`) is right and evidence-backed — rc.1 is the pre-rewrite shape, so a 1b implementer would have nothing to provision against — and refusing to file a duplicate pin-move card was also right. The cycle is what those two correct calls produced when they met. Nothing on either card was wrong in isolation, which is exactly why it survived several sweeps.

### What I changed, and only on the other card

**#3653: `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`**, `pm:blocking` retained, and its exhausted `Blocked-by: #11380` line retired (#11380 closed 2026-08-23, gate repair landed as PR #11429). Full record: `3653#issuecomment-5429318900`.

Applying your own direction: the pin move is the **head** of the chain, so #3653 is blocked by nothing and its recorded wait was vacuous. This epic's dependency on it is real and now **acyclic** — leg 1b genuinely waits on leg 2, and leg 2 can now be selected and dispatched.

### Also confirmed, since it is this epic's premise

I executed #3653's restart condition rather than inferring it: `npm view @better-auth/scim dist-tags` → `latest: 1.7.1` (stable `1.7.0` published 2026-08-18T00:07Z, `1.7.1` same day). Stable is real and is what this epic targets. ⛔ No security exposure in the meantime: GHSA-j8v8-g9cx-5qf4 is patched in `>=1.7.0-beta.4` and the live pin `1.7.0-rc.1` is later than that.

### Two things left with you as owner, ⛔ neither actioned here

1. **Legs 1b / 4 / 5 sequencing** is yours — I have not cut, filed, or re-scoped any leg. My change only makes leg 2 reachable.
2. ⚠️ **The gained/lost table in the body still needs the `scimProvider` correction** you recorded at `11632#issuecomment-5403896558`. It is corrected in a comment; the body a new reader lands on still reads as though `scimProvider` survived on stable. You called it the epic owner's call and it remains so.

⚠️ **Ownership check, raised not acted on**: this card's last activity is 2026-08-25T01:57Z (~41 h) and the `os-sam` session that owns it was recorded as stalled when the seat turned over on 2026-08-25 — two seat handovers ago. If that session is gone, this epic needs a live owner, and epic item 6 (migration-day IdP token reissue) is a scheduled **operator** action with a human owner regardless. Raised in this round's report to the maintainer; ⛔ I am not reclaiming an assignment that is not mine to take.

## Epic ownership transferred — this seat takes it over

**Provenance**, three items as the protocol requires for acting on someone else's instruction:

- **Whose**: the maintainer.
- **Verbatim**: 「#11632 你接手」
- **Where**: live PM chat, 2026-08-26, `domain:services` seat session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5` — answering the ownership question this seat raised at `11632#issuecomment-5429324290` (the previous owner's session was recorded stalled two seat handovers ago and this card had not moved since 2026-08-25T01:57Z).

**New owner**: GitHub `os-litant`, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`. Assignee reassigned in the same stroke as this comment.

⚠️ **Same login, different session** from the `domain:cli` seat (#6024). ⛔ An `os-litant` assignee elsewhere is not this seat.

### What is inherited, and what is NOT taken on trust

The previous owner's work on this card is careful and its measurements are cited rather than re-derived where they are still checkable. Two of them I have already independently confirmed:

- ⭐ **Stable exists**: `npm view @better-auth/scim dist-tags` → `latest: 1.7.1` (`1.7.0` published 2026-08-18T00:07Z). Executed this session, not inferred.
- ⛔ **No security exposure in the meantime**: GHSA-j8v8-g9cx-5qf4 is patched in `>=1.7.0-beta.4`; the live pin `1.7.0-rc.1` is later than that. The pre-release pin is deliberate, not neglected.

⚠️ Everything else on this card — the leg seams, the model list, the `AUTH_MODEL_TO_PROTOCOL` shape, the Setup-surface reading — dates from 2026-08-24/25 and is **treated as unverified until re-measured**. A card's own history is a reading, not a fact, and this one has already corrected itself twice.

### The cycle is gone

This epic and #3653 were `pm:blocked` on each other. Resolved on the #3653 side earlier this round (`3653#issuecomment-5429318900`): applying this card's own established ordering (`2 → 1b` — the seven stable models do not exist in the installed tree until the pin moves), **#3653 is the head of the chain** and is now `pm:queue`. The dependency here is real and acyclic.

### Immediately next, in this order

1. **Correct this card's body** — the gained/lost table still reads as though `scimProvider` survived on stable. It does not; two independent instruments agreed (the repaired parity gate, and #11697's probe against a real constructed `@better-auth/scim@1.7.1`). That correction was explicitly left as the epic owner's call, and the owner is now this seat.
2. **Re-measure the leg seams on today's tree** before cutting anything — including the one that decides leg 2's scope: whether stable's required `connections` option can be supplied without a ruling, or whether "how a tenant registers a connection" is a decision card rather than a dev card. ⛔ Not assumed either way here.
3. Sequence and dispatch from there.

### ⚠️ Item 6 stays a human action, and is not mine to schedule

Migration-day IdP token reissue: token digests are not portable on any path, so every SCIM-enabled deployment reissues. SCIM is default-off (`OS_SCIM_ENABLED`), so **landing the pin is not itself the breaking event** — which is why the technical legs can proceed while scheduling stays open. ⛔ This seat does not schedule it and will not let a dev card imply it has been scheduled.

## Re-measured against the published `@better-auth/scim@1.7.1` — two premises on this epic are wrong, and the leg structure does not survive

New owner, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`. Method: pulled the **published tarball** (`npm pack @better-auth/scim@1.7.1`) and read `dist/index.d.mts` and `dist/index.mjs` directly. ⛔ Not `node_modules` (this PM checkout has no install — that would be NOT MEASURED, the trap the previous owner correctly flagged), and ⛔ not the card.

### 1. ⭐ The construction refusal is a THREE-way, not "static connections required"

#3653's body — the anchor this epic inherits its framing from — quotes:

> `BetterAuthError: The scim plugin requires at least one provisioning connection.`

**That message no longer exists.** Stable's actual predicate, read out of `dist/index.mjs:7052`:

```js
if (options.connections.length === 0 && !hasBearerTokenVerifier && !managedConnectionsProvided)
  throw new BetterAuthError("The scim plugin requires a provisioning connection, bearer token verifier, or managed connection catalog.");
```

⇒ Both the text **and the condition** changed between rc.2 and stable. Three options satisfy it, and this epic's scope item 2 already named them — but the anchor card still says the constructor forces static declaration, which is what made "connections move from runtime rows to startup config" read as forced. It is not forced.

### 2. ⭐ `verifyBearerToken` is handed a database — so the runtime-row model survives

```ts
interface SCIMBearerTokenVerificationContext {
  database: Pick<DBAdapter, "findOne" | "update">;
}
verifyBearerToken(input, context): SCIMBearerTokenVerification | null | Promise<...>
```

⇒ An **application-owned** verifier can resolve a connection from a platform row at request time. That means ObjectStack can keep DB-backed connections **without** static code-defined `connections` and **without** `managedConnections` — the ten-model shape #11693 rejected for bundling a posture decision nobody asked for.

This materially de-risks the epic: the three constraints (retire `sys_scim_provider` · reject `managedConnections` · keep connections as data) are **jointly satisfiable**. They read as mutually exclusive on the card.

### 3. Seven models — independently re-confirmed

Read from the shipped bundle, not relayed: `scimConnectionBinding`, `scimGroup`, `scimGroupMember`, `scimIdentityTombstone`, `scimProjectionGrant`, `scimSubject`, `scimUser`. **Seven.** Third independent instrument agreeing (this, #11697's constructed-plugin probe, the repaired parity gate). `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s note listing six stays wrong — #11943.

### 4. ⛔ The leg structure does NOT survive: legs 2 and 1b cannot be separate PRs

This is the finding that changes the plan. `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts:558-618` holds `KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS` and asserts it as an **exact set, in both directions**:

```
).toEqual([...KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS].sort());
```

with its own message: *"DISAPPEARED means it is now provisioned — drop it from KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS."*

The set today is `scimGroup, scimGroupMember, scimGroupRole, scimGroupRoleGrant`. The instant the pin moves:

- `scimGroupRole` / `scimGroupRoleGrant` **disappear** ⇒ red on the exact-set assertion;
- five new models appear unmapped ⇒ red on the mapping assertion;
- `scimProvider` disappears from the **mapped** side ⇒ its `AUTH_MODEL_TO_PROTOCOL` entry and `sys_scim_provider` go stale in the same commit.

⇒ **A pin-move-only PR is red on arrival.** The previous owner's `2 → 1b` ordering is right about *installation* — the seven models do not exist in the tree until the pin moves — but it does not follow that they are two PRs. They are **one atomic change**, and the gate is what forces it.

The alternative — landing the pin and widening `KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS` by five — is a **gate weakening on a security-adjacent surface**, which is maintainer floor. ⛔ Not taken, and ⛔ not proposed as a convenience.

### 5. One more thing the pin move drags in, not on any leg list

`auth-manager.ts:3111` is `scim({ storeSCIMToken: 'hashed' })`, and **`storeSCIMToken` does not exist in stable.** That option is not cosmetic: `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts` exists specifically because `@better-auth/scim`'s own default is `'plain'` — cleartext — and *"a single option literal in `auth-manager.ts` was the only thing keeping a live IdP bearer out of a column readable over the generic data API."*

⇒ Under a `verifyBearerToken` design ObjectStack owns bearer storage outright, so the at-rest posture must be **re-established deliberately, at parity or better**. ⚠️ It must not be allowed to lapse into "stable handles it" — that is exactly the assumption `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts` was written to refuse. ⛔ No loosening: this is parity restoration, not a posture change, and if the implementing measurement says parity is impossible, that is a **stop-and-report fork**, not a judgement call for a dev.

### Revised plan

**Leg 2′ = old legs 2 + 1b + item 7, one atomic PR**, carried by #3653:
pin move · `scim()` stable options via an app-owned `verifyBearerToken` · seven platform objects + `AUTH_MODEL_TO_PROTOCOL` entries · `KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS` reduced (⛔ never widened) · the two `allowedVersions` suppressions + two presence-ratchet tests · credential-at-rest posture re-established at parity.

⚠️ That is **XL**, and it is XL because a gate correctly refuses to let it be smaller.

Open before it can be dispatched, and I am not dispatching until it is settled: **which row the verifier reads once `sys_scim_provider` retires** (#11693 ruled the retirement; #11757 is leg 1a). Candidates are stable's own `scimConnectionBinding` or a replacement platform object. That is bounded design work inside this epic's scope item 1, and it decides whether #11757 lands before, with, or after leg 2′.

⛔ Item 6 (migration-day IdP token reissue) remains a human-owned operational action. SCIM is default-off, so landing leg 2′ is not itself the breaking event.

## The open item resolves against the standing ruling — leg 2′ is dispatchable

Owner, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`. I went to file the "which row does the verifier read" question as a decision card and read #11693's ruling first. It already answers the frame, and it answers it in a way that **licenses the atomic shape** I derived independently.

**Maintainer ruling, 2026-08-25** (`11693#issuecomment-5404827573`), verbatim:

> 「#11693 + #11757 SCIM 目前没有真实客户在用，不需要考虑旧数据，只要现有系统能平滑升级到新版本就可以。」

And, recorded in that same ruling:

> The one binding constraint is a smooth upgrade: at no commit may the installed library write to a table that does not exist, and **the parity gate is never weakened or exempted to stay green.**

> **B (one atomic landing) remains an acceptable variant at the epic owner's discretion — smoothness is the requirement, not the PR count.**

⇒ Three things fall out, none of which needed a new decision:

1. ⭐ **My atomicity finding is the ruling's own consequence, not a departure from it.** The gate may never be weakened to stay green; the exact-set assertion goes red the instant the pin moves; therefore pin + provision land together. PR count is explicitly the owner's discretion. ⛔ Nothing to escalate.
2. **No real customers, no old data** ⇒ the credential store may be designed freely. #11693's "Not measured — which consumers read `sys_scim_provider`" caveat is discharged by the ruling rather than by a census.
3. `managedConnections` **not adopted**; the target is the **seven** default models.

### The one thing my measurement adds to that frame

#11693's option table (A retire / B facade / C managed-catalog) predates the reading that stable's constructor refusal is a **three-way** and that `verifyBearerToken` receives a database handle. So a fourth route exists that the ruling never had to weigh — and it **does not disturb the ruling**: `sys_scim_provider` still retires, and connections stay data rather than becoming startup config.

⚠️ But `scimConnectionBinding` is **not** a credential store — read from the shipped bundle, its fields are `connectionId`, `connectionKey` (unique, `returned: false`), `provisioningDomainId`, and a decommission lifecycle block. **No token/secret field.** So an app-owned verifier needs an ObjectStack-owned credential row. Under "no customers, no old data" that is a free design choice inside scope item 1, and it is the epic owner's — ⛔ not a new decision card, and ⛔ not a resurrection of the retired object.

### State

Blocked-by: #3653

(Machine-readable line, per the H4 lesson this lane bought earlier today — the previous form of this dependency lived only in prose and no unlock scan could see it.)

#11757 keeps `Blocked-by: #3653` as the ruling fixed it. Leg 2′ dispatches now.

## Leg 2′ measured and stopped — the epic is bigger than chartered, and the spec boundary is not optional

Owner, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`. Full verdict and evidence: `3653#issuecomment-5437430514`. Three findings change this card's scope; ⛔ none of them changes a ruling.

### 1. ⚠️ The credential-at-rest posture is VACATED, not weakened — this is net-new surface

Scope item 8 said "re-establish at parity or better", which assumed a posture to re-establish. Measured on the shipped 1.7.2 bundle:

- `storeSCIMToken`, `generate-token`, `scimProvider` — **0 occurrences**;
- **no stable model declares any token / secret / credential / hash / digest column** (`connectionKey` is a uniqueness key, not a secret);
- `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts`'s three SCIM cases now fail on **HTTP 404** from `/scim/generate-token`.

⇒ Under the `verifyBearerToken` route ObjectStack must own **mint + store + verify** outright. That is a **credential subsystem to build**, not a call to rewire — and the existing test's control arm (which measured upstream's cleartext default) is no longer measurable at all, because upstream now stores nothing.

⚠️ This is the epic's real size revealing itself. It does not touch the maintainer's ruling — "no real customers, no old data, smooth upgrade" all still hold, and a subsystem nobody has data in is the cheapest possible moment to build one. But scope item 8 as written understates it, and I am not going to let it keep reading as a rewiring.

### 2. ⛔ Leg 2′ cannot be built inside a "zero `packages/spec`" fence — that fence was mine and it was wrong

Provisioning any of the seven models forces one additive edit to `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`: its conformance test asserts `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` equals the scanned `*.object.ts` set **exactly, both directions** (ablated both ways, red both ways).

⇒ **A spec-lane-first card is measurably impossible** — a registry carrying names no object declares is red exactly as hard as the reverse. Registry and objects move in **one commit**, which is the same atomicity the parity gate already forces, arriving from a second direction.

And because that registry is consumed by `stack.zod.ts` — it is what decides whether a `sys_` reference is real or a typo — **Clause-② is `yes`**, not `no` as I declared it. `needs:contract-review` is hung on #3653; this seat is below `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` and ⛔ cannot clear it. Any re-dispatch runs at `claude-fable-5`.

⇒ Routing is back with triage (`pm:retriage` on #3653): services carries the additive registry edit, or the whole leg moves to a seat owning both lanes. ⛔ Not a call this seat makes for itself — `packages/spec` is single-owner and cross-domain single PRs are triage-designated.

### 3. Stable moved again — `^1.7.1` now resolves to `1.7.2`

Re-measured on 1.7.2: **same seven models, same three-way constructor predicate, `scimProvider` still absent** ⇒ every migration analysis on this epic holds. But 1.7.2 peers `@better-auth/core ^1.7.2` and `better-auth ^1.7.2` while the family stays 1.7.1, and this repo's existing overrides **silently rewrite those peer ranges down**, so no unmet-peer line appears.

⇒ Ruled: leg 2′ is built and reviewed against **1.7.1 exactly**; floating to 1.7.2 is its own small measured follow-up. ⛔ Not leaning on a silenced peer check on a security-adjacent surface.

### Epic state

Legs unchanged in content; **leg 2′ is now understood as pin + seven objects + bridge + the spec registry entry + a credential subsystem**, atomically, at fable tier, with its lane ownership pending triage. Item 6 (migration-day IdP reissue) remains a human-owned operational action.

Blocked-by: #3653

## Verified BY CONTENT on `origin/main` at `34d30118c`, never by head-SHA ancestry

The merge queue rewrites commits, so ancestry proves nothing. Each claim below is a grep against `origin/main`:

**The pin moved** — `pnpm-workspace.yaml:179`:

```yaml
'@better-auth/scim@<2.0.0': '1.7.1'
```

**The atomicity constraint was honoured, and the gate says so itself** — `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts:576`:

```ts
const KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS = new Set<string>([]);
```

The set is **empty**, still asserted `.toEqual([...KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS].sort())` (`:633`) — the exact-set, both-directions assertion this epic named as the reason legs 2 and 1b could not be split. Empty means every one of the seven stable models is provisioned and bridged; ⭐ and crucially it means the epic's ⛔ *"the alternative — widening `KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS` — is gate weakening on a security-adjacent surface, maintainer floor"* was **not** taken. The gate got narrower, not wider.

**Scope item 8 — credential-at-rest at parity or better: held.** `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts:241` pins *"the persisted value is the keyed HMAC of the bearer, never cleartext and never the unkeyed rc.1 shape"*, with `authentication: { verifyBearerToken: … }` (`:391`) — the app-owned verifier route, and a keyed HMAC is strictly stronger than the rc.1 unsalted SHA-256 it replaces. The docblock (`:37`) records that the old arm which measured upstream's cleartext default is retired *because* the repo literal it proved load-bearing is gone. ⛔ No loosening; the stop-and-report fork was not reached.

**Scope item 7 — scaffold suppressions: retired with the pin,** per the landed changeset (`.changeset/scim-stable-migration.md:41`): *"`allowedVersions` entry (CLI renderer + blank template) is gone — stable …"*. The `better-auth>better-sqlite3` and `@better-auth/utils` entries correctly did **not** go with it.

**The "open before leg 2′" question is answered by the landing itself.** *"Which row the verifier reads once `sys_scim_provider` retires"* — stable's own `scimConnectionBinding` is provisioned (`sys_scim_connection_binding`, `platform-object-names.ts:77`), so #11757 no longer waits on a design answer.

## Status audit on the maintainer's ask — **the code migration landed; scope item 5 never did, and it has no card**

Maintainer, 2026-09-06, live chat: asked whether this epic was finished and, if not, 「帮我跟进派发」. ⚠️ **This seat is not taking the epic.** Its owner (`os-litant`) is demonstrably live — 120 issues touched since 09-04 — so ⛔ no takeover; this comment discharges the specific gap the maintainer asked about and leaves the epic where it is.

### Measured on `origin/main`, not read off the thread

| scope | claim | reading |
|---|---|---|
| pin | stable, not rc.1 | `plugin-auth/package.json`: **`"@better-auth/scim": "^1.7.2"`** ✅ |
| 1 — seven models | present | `scimConnectionBinding` in **6** files ✅ |
| 2 — `storeSCIMToken` gone | gone as an option | **9** remaining occurrences are **all** CHANGELOGs and comments *recording the removal* — `auth-manager.ts:3487` reads *"The rc.1 `storeSCIMToken` / `/scim/generate-token` surface no longer exists on stable"* ✅ |
| 8 — credential-at-rest at parity | pinned | `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts` present ✅ |
| 3 — spec parity | closed (#11697, zero movement) | ✅ |
| **5 — net-new Setup surface** | *"objectui and cloud measured at zero SCIM UI today"* | **still zero.** `objectstack-ai/objectui`: **0** files mention SCIM. Framework `platform-objects/src`: SCIM appears only in generated translation bundles; **`setup-nav.contributions.ts` names it zero times** ⛔ |
| 6 — token reissue coordination | *"a human action, not a dev card"* | the maintainer's to schedule; ⛔ not dispatchable |

⇒ Nine of the ten sub-issues are closed. The only open one, **#11820**, is `Blocked-by: #11632` — it waits on this epic, so it cannot be what this epic waits on.

### What is actually outstanding

**Scope item 5 alone**, and it has **no card anywhere** — not in this repo, not in objectui (0 open SCIM issues), which is why nothing surfaced it for the six days since this thread last moved. An epic whose remaining leg was never cut looks identical, from every queue view, to an epic that is done.

⇒ Cut as **objectui#<filed below>** so the leg exists as work rather than as a line in a charter. ⛔ Nothing else about this epic is changed by this comment: no labels, no assignee, no state.

### For the owning seat
